39.6: And when they cannot, he shall be as a prince who saith unto God: I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof; those who are commanded by Thy word, and one singleness is exalted.
39.7: And then shall he be who sought judgement by faith, and was ashamed from the reproach of faith; likewise shall he be who believeth and standeth firm at the time of the Holy One.
39.8: And when he who cannot draw near leaveth the offering in humility and in lowliness and in faith, he taketh that which the prince took, an hundred; and concerning this it is fitting for the faithful, when he draweth near or draweth not near, that he be in fear and in trembling, until Christ ascendeth from upon the altar; and the ascension — when the body is fulfilled, all his body shall be fulfilled, and he shall ascend; today he proceedeth from the body; and after this, when he stood before the ascension, they cannot set upon him the might of the Holy Spirit, which He sent upon His disciples after the ascension; and if he is he who in the time of giving — all — and went out before the ascension of Christ — and the ascension shall be to him from the portion of Judas Iscariot, who said concerning him, and the holy Gospel, that he is he who in the night of the day of Friday, the night in which Christ gave unto His disciples from His body and His blood, forsook the apostles and went out alone, before Christ came forth; and then Satan entered unto him, when he went out before the holy offering was fulfilled.
39.9: For the holy Gospel said that he was present, and went out then; and the disciples abode with Christ, until he went out, and went out with him.
39.10: And likewise he who goeth out before the ascension of Christ from the house of the Christians became in the likeness of Judas.
39.11: And if it be a great house, a work it is not fitting for them to go out.
39.12: And he who is in earnest at the time of the Mass, and goeth not out until the offering ascendeth from the altar, taketh the crown that keepeth, which we have mentioned unto thee before.
39.13: And by the faith of the priests who ordained a law unto Christ — and they cannot know to declare the books — he shall be driven, he who willed, from the law, before the offering ascendeth from the altar.
39.14: And they perish, their souls, and the soul of all the people; for God commanded men that they should hear the commandment of the priests, if they command them in that which is commanded.
39.15: And when they transgress them, they take destruction for ever.
39.16: As the hosts of the Devil: and when men heard the commandment of the Devil for their head, and obeyed him in that which God breaketh, and were kept back from the praises and the holiness, and went out with him, unto for ever.
39.17: Likewise shall fall and perish everyone who goeth out from the house of the Christians, by wrath the priests shall drive him out, before the offering is fulfilled.
39.18: And if they hear concerning them, in that which God promiseth not, they take judgement with them, as the hosts of the Devil were judged with him; likewise he who holdeth back at the time of the Holy One, and heareth not the declaration of the books and of the holiness, and is adorned, taketh judgement upon me; for he is, instead of him who runneth for Christ, they polish him; for he is he who taketh by an unclean spirit and an unclean body.
39.19: And thou art he: as the books and the holiness made them hosts before the offering, they sanctify the faithful, and His ascension they cleanse, as I have shown thee; and after this it is fitting to take the offering, as men cannot be, who are without sin, for one hour that abideth in the wilderness alone.
39.20: And he who shall be joined with men, causing to sin, burneth from her by a word which is not fitting; or by an oath, or by reviling, or by a curse of his neighbour.
39.21: Or by withholding from this: he is he who in these works abode, and was defiled, and was cleansed; and he wisheth for the hearing of the reading of the books, and the hearing of the prayer of light, that he may cast away his defilement, and be sanctified.
39.22: And after this he eateth and drinketh from the holy flesh and the blood of Christ; and he is holy, and is converted; and he who loveth not the books and the holiness, and is confounded, shall be reckoned — his body shall be reckoned, and his blood is for Christ; and he also is unclean.
39.23: And Christ shall humble him again exceedingly; He said in the tongue of the prophet: Be humbled; for He said in the tongue of the prophet: Be humbled; for him who humbleth me I will exalt, and I will honour him who honoured me; and He swore this, as the likeness of him who soweth seed in earth which is not watered, and plougheth it not; he also destroyeth the seed, and it sprouteth not for the earth.
39.24: Likewise men, if he was in fatherhood, sought thee, as thou sowest for thee: he shall be as earth, a thing of many defilements; and if he come into the house of Kerkemtedan, and hear the voice of their books, and the Gospel, the voice of God — the water of life — as the LORD God said; and he is watered by that water from newness, that cleanseth sin.
39.25: And when he is watered, and Tesfa cometh, the Holy Spirit descendeth upon him, and cleanseth him from sin, as earth is cleansed from defilement.
39.26: And then he receiveth the holy offering, and beareth fruit in him, as earth that is opened, the chosen one, that beareth the seed that is sown, and it beareth fruit in it.
39.27: Behold, I have shown thee the glory and the holiness which is equal upon all the faithful; and apart from Him they cannot do anything at all from the commandment of God; for by the glory the Holy Spirit abideth in them, and the unclean spirits are driven out from them, and they are made to do the work for God.
39.28: And whoso departeth from going unto the house of the Christians in the morning and in the evening, and departeth from their prayer at the time of the Holy One, as I have told thee, and reacheth death in that day, and shall be reckoned for ever and ever — as the Devil and his hosts fell from her — and behold, I have shown thee the glory and the holiness, that it is fitting upon all the faithful, all of them, at all the days of their life.
39.29: For God hath appointed for them these works — they are the cause of their salvation and of what is their life; and this is it: that in every day and in every night, seven and two hours, God appointed for them three times to reach unto the gate of the house of the Christians, in the morning, and in the evening, and at the time of the Holy One; and these three times at which the Christian reacheth unto the gate are not the measure of two hours; and there remaineth for them seven and two hours, in which they do the work of the flesh that passeth away; and God giveth them from the wealth of this world a doubled reward, in place of the work which they forsook, in place of those two hours, while it is charged unto them upon that which cleanseth them, for the life of their souls — which is His glory, of God, and His holiness, and the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them, and the forgiveness of their sins.
39.30: And likewise in every week, seven days, God hath appointed upon men their work, that it rule not over him.
39.31: And He said unto them: Work ye the work of the flesh two days, and work ye for the spirit one day.
39.32: And in that one day, work ye in it the work that is spiritual, from morning until evening; it shall be for you in it a work without reading the word of God in the holy house of the Christians. And He said again: When thou readest, a good reading read. And all who are gathered unto thee, and thou doest for them, God shall give thee a reward on their account, in the kingdom.

40.1: And if thou knowest not, thou shalt not do; go not unto another city, until thou shalt see that which abideth for thee; as thou goest, thou seekest the work of this world in the district which hath no sacrifice, unto the other which hath a sacrifice.
40.2: And the day of the life of the Spirit passeth from thee without work; because thou knowest not, that thou — until the other day — shalt not, that thou mayest find the life of thy spirit; verily God commanded that He do not the work of this world on the day of rest; therefore that men should forsake every thing, and abide in the holy books, which are the spiritual life, and should pray over it without delay, and be occupied in labours, as he doeth the border of eternal life; for the reading of the books of God cleanseth the soul and the body, and they are cleansed from sin, in the portion for His disciples, in the holy Gospel; verily it is a vineyard, and its fathers withered, and every ordinance that beareth not fruit and dieth is done; and that which beareth fruit is it that is cleansed, as He created many, and it was fulfilled.
40.3: Behold, I have shown thee in this word which I have told you therein.
40.4: It is shown: they shall spring up; men shall be cleansed from all of it, and shall bear fruit, the fruit of eternal life.
40.5: And he who heareth not the word, and speaketh not His books continually, shall be without fruit; and his Father cutteth him off from the burden of the Son, as they cut off the branch from the vineyard.
40.6: And he who speaketh the books continually on the holy day, he abideth in Christ, as the branch abideth in the vineyard; for the cleansing of Christ cleanseth him, and sanctifieth him from his sin, and causeth him to bear — he beareth — the fruit of eternal life.
40.7: Beloved, this — and for the rest which we have mentioned, the hours of the faithful; and in them they shall overcome the satans — which is our going unto the house of the Christians in the morning and in the evening, at every time; and we tarry at the time of the Holy One without ceasing, from the, until it is fulfilled.
40.8: And the hearing of the books of God on the holy day — all of it, and unto the rest; if men work continually, He abideth, in it the Holy Spirit; and he shall be continually who is born of God; and there shall not be over him the hosts of sin.
40.9: As John the evangelist said in the epistle: For everyone who is born of God sinneth not; for his seed abideth firm, and he cannot sin; for he is born of God.
40.10: And again he said in it: He who is born of God keepeth himself, and the evil one draweth not near to touch him.
40.11: And all the faithful who are baptized — they are born of God — as the seed of the Holy Spirit abideth firm in them, by which they are born of God; and He keepeth them from the evil one and from the hosts; and they cannot sin; but they do good, without their desire; for the Holy Spirit worketh for them over him; for He is firm in them; and He loveth to abide in them; if he keepeth these commandments, He abideth in them, and keepeth them from the evil one; and they have no power to sin, for the Holy Spirit hindereth them from sin, and keepeth them from the evil one who draweth them into the doing of sin.
40.12: And if they sin by weakness, then the Holy Spirit who dwelleth in them taketh them, and draweth them unto shame by leave; and likewise if they forsake one of these three commandments, the Holy Spirit forsaketh them, and an unclean, evil spirit overcometh them, and draweth them unto the doing of sin, by work and by violence; and God shall not be in them, if it be so; knowledge: he who is born of God sinneth not.
40.13: As John the apostle said: Behold, what is the greatness from these commandments, by which it shall be that men delight with Christ, the Son of God, in the glory of the kingdom; and he shall be who is born of God.
40.14: And they are not fat, and are not drunk, and have no weariness; and sweat perisheth not as and thirst; and sweat perisheth not; for he is he who from of old goeth to the work of this world; he goeth forth unto the house of the Christians; and after its fulfilment, work — he goeth unto her in the evening; and sweat perisheth not.
40.15: And at the time of the Holy One, if all — all — at every time, its measure is as one hour.
40.16: From seven and seven hours — and there is not in this again a — in those festivals they shall find the seeking of eternal life in the kingdom of heaven; and God giveth a doubled [reward] instead of that which they have left in those two other days, concerning the trading of the holy day; for fatness is grace; it is in His fatness.
40.17: As He said in the tongue of the prophet: I who slew, and I make alive; I am He who burneth; I who smote, and I heal; whom I heal.
40.18: But He giveth unto men a double [reward] instead of that which they have left from the work of this world, as He said in the holy Gospel — He said: Be ye not anxious for that which ye shall eat, and for that which ye shall drink; for all this do the nations seek; and your Father who is in heaven knoweth that ye are in need of all this, of which ye are needy; but this [seek ye] first: the kingdom and the righteousness; and it shall be given unto you a double [reward] instead of that which was left from us, for the sake of this seeking, that took the kingdom and the righteousness; and it shall be given unto us a double [reward] instead of that which is without the reading of the word of God, first; for He is the Father of us all, and He is He who giveth us that which is fitting, and that which is fitting, and that which is fitting; for He knoweth that we desire — we seek all this; He giveth unto us the kingdom; and He reckoneth unto us all this; He is He who giveth unto us; for He is He who, as we are humbled, strengtheneth us for this temporal world. Behold, beloved: these three commandments, keep them; for they are the salvation of everyone who believeth in Christ; and in them they overcome the evil enemy, who is he who prevaileth over them; and they have no power over him, without these three commandments.
40.19: For in them the Holy Spirit abideth firm in them, and strengtheneth them against the evil host, and they overcome him, while they are upon the earth in the flesh.
40.20: And after their going forth from the flesh, He giveth them victory over the hosts of the Devil in the air, and saveth them — joy and life for ever.
40.21: And the evil one, moreover — when he knew that these three commandments are they, a fence for the faithful, and in them they overcome him — and he proceedeth against them in their, and hindereth the enemy, and troubleth them from them, until he separate them from her, and the Holy Spirit forsaketh them, and he prevaileth over them, and destroyeth them.
40.22: And they, moreover, beloved, shall burn in faith; readiness shall be with them, as a wall, that they may receive in it the buckler, the darts of Satan and his spears shall trouble them from them — the commandments.
40.23: As the apostle Paul said in the epistle to the people of Ephesus: Take ye the sword of the Holy Spirit, which is the word of God, in all those [times], and in all, while ye pray at every time in the Holy Spirit; and be watchful over this, at every time.
40.24: I show that the word of God, which abideth in it — or which abideth upon him — and His glory and His holiness continually, is the sword of the Holy Spirit, which is in truth.

41.1: For men — if he keepeth the three commandments — but they are fat; and the giving of the Mass and the work shall be, by the Holy Spirit, firm in him; and he is the sword of God: when the hosts of Satan see him, they flee from him, and cannot draw near unto him; and they resist, and they accuse men, those who transgress one of these three commandments and forsake it; the Holy Spirit is resisted over him; as with a man who hath in his hand a sharp sword, polished: his enemies cannot draw near unto him, from fear of the sword; and they stand from afar, and they cast at him with stones and sling-stones; and the sword falleth from his hand; and they cry out unto him; and he also desireth that there be in his hand a shield, with the sword; and when they cast at him with stones, he receiveth them therein, and it falleth from his hand.
41.2: And thy shield is faith, by which a man can keep these three commandments; the satans shall not draw near unto it, who trouble them from her.
41.3: As Paul saith in his epistle to the men of Ephesus:
41.4: Seek the shield of faith, which is the sword of the Holy Spirit, by which the quenching of all his arrows of the evil one, which are full of fire, is possible.
41.5: It is shown that men cannot be joined unto the glory and the holiness and the speaking of the word of God — which is the sword of the Holy Spirit — if there be not with him the shield of faith, by which he destroyeth the arrows of the evil one.
41.6: And I also show thee the arrows, that by them he overcometh, if he believeth, if he keepeth the three commandments. The first arrow: when a man who believeth goeth unto the house of the Christians for the glory and for the Mass and for the speaking of the word of God, Satan aimeth at him the work of this world, and stoppeth [it] in his breath, that he is he who, if he went unto the house of the Christians and tarried for the passing, shall pass from him the likeness, thus and thus, and causeth him to lose the profit.
41.7: And when he heareth from Satan this counsel, and transgresseth that which is meet for him, the sword falleth from his hand, which is the Holy Spirit; and if it be that his possession is the shield of faith, it is not bent for Satan, a portion for that which he adorned for him from the work of this world, and that which he strengthened in his handful from the lost profit of the likeness — those who give him say: Christ, thy fathers, righteousness is departed from thee; he saith: I will not forsake my likeness to pass away, and I will not let my work perish, that which passed me. For he is he who saith: Seek first my kingdom and my righteousness, and all this shall be added unto you. And if he believeth thus, he overcometh the thought of Satan by the shield of faith; and he is joined unto the glory and unto the Mass and the reading, firm — the sword in his hand — and overcometh thereby his enemy; and he shall be a counsel that is greater than the counsels of the martyrs, who endured their strife with the flesh, or in their likeness. And his strife, this one, is with the hosts of Satan, spirits of fire, who have dominion over all the earth, as Paul saith; and his counsel, at that time, is greater than the counsels of the martyrs; for he stood firm and burned with the helps of the satans, and the roughness of those who burned the martyrs.
41.8: Behold, I have shown thee the first arrow; and this is the second arrow: If a man wisheth to be joined in the speaking on the holy day, and goeth unto the house of the Christians for the glory and for the Mass, every time, and feareth Satan, and speaketh: Let us not find in the way, one draweth near unto thee thus and thus, lest he delay thee, or crush thee, or kill thee; and if he hearkened from him, and despiseth that which is meet for him, he forsaketh the Holy Spirit, who is the sword, and Satan his enemy resisteth over him, and destroyeth him. If there was with him the shield of faith, he giveth him and saith unto him: The lying Satan cannot at all delay me, and crush me, and torment me, and kill me, without the will of Christ, my strength; and if He willed it, He would do it by me.
41.9: And when thou didst hide thyself in a cave of the earth, he cometh not unto thee, and my doth not rise to work by thee; he cannot at all work evil by thee. And when it was thus, I was lifted up above the beasts; for the hairs of my head are numbered.
41.10: And he is in this [way]; and he is he who saith thus: For two sparrows are sold for two farthings; and one of them falleth not, saith He, to the earth, without the will of your Father who is in heaven.
41.11: And unto you also, all the hairs of your head are numbered; and he is, by this shield of faith, he who overcometh his enemy, and is resisted over him; and the sword abideth in his hand, which is the Holy Spirit; and there shall be a reward in this.
41.12: The second is greater than the first.
41.13: For he is he who gave over his head unto Christ, exceedingly, more than the martyrs; and he endured the tree of His cross, and followed Him, and believed; for they who kill him and destroy him are those who are without Him; and behold, I have shown thee the second arrow. The arrow of the veil: and when it was for a man — from a work that is done by it, from the keeping of these three commandments, and the fear which they fear for him by it, for Satan, until they are cut off from the veil.
41.14: And Satan cometh upon him secretly, and presseth upon him, until the sword falleth from his hand, and he resisteth over him; and the sin of this boaster, from sinners, is a sin; for he is he who was exalted, and was lifted up from the speaking and the glory and the Mass, without a cause.

42.1: And if his pretext became the purity of the faith — it is this which driveth Satan, weakened, away from him; and he saith unto his soul: Thou hadst power, O Satan, to cast me down — and not by deed.
42.2: He wisheth now that he may cast me down in weakness and in destruction — the destruction wherein he himself fell from heaven; for Satan and his hosts, when they were shut out from the glory of God and from His holiness, and were troubled and troubled exceedingly — or else they desired sin — [were cast down] from the kingdom of heaven; and He created me, that I might inherit their kingdom, from which they fell; and if thou troublest me [to depart] from His glory and His holiness, and from the reading of the books of God, and troublest me even as they [were troubled], I fall from Him, even as they fell.
42.3: And by this thought of good — which is the purity of the faith — he overcometh them, and doeth that which is fitting for him [to do] before the glory of God and His holiness and the reading of His books; and he is joined in fellowship with His martyrs who were slain; and he overcame, and took the crown of victory, and the kingdom of heaven abideth with Christ in the kingdom which endureth for ever.
42.4: And know, friend, that by these three cords Satan entereth into the believer at all times and at every hour, that he may trouble them and bring them unto the three commands; and he striveth not to cease from the crown of victory, nor shall the kingdom of heaven be fitting for them; and know: he who is fought against departeth by one of all the cords, and overcometh, and goeth unto the house of the Christians, with more joy than [the joy] which is without fighting; and the believer is fitting, that he be guarded, and that he keep for the time; and he causeth men to stumble by stumbling from these three cords; and from him, at one time, there cometh a hearing from him, and glory at all times.
42.5: Upon him, in the assembly: from him he feareth not; and if he heareth not — from him he feareth not; and if he heareth not, that he should turn back unto him: for he is not able to dwell in the fence, and he rebuketh not in it a second time; for by a sniffing he snorteth; and if he snort once, and there entered a fence into it, he leaveth not always from dwelling.
42.6: And concerning this the apostles commanded the believers, and ordained for them: for unto you [belong] the prayers of the morning and the prayers of the evening; these are the prayers — at the second [hour], and at the third, and at the fourth hour, and at the hour of the evening meal, and in the spirit of the evening meal.
42.7: These three prayers are added upon those prayers; they are fitting for them, [to pray] wheresoever they will.
42.8: Until there is for them no work: they are fitting for them in unity and in deed.
42.9: And again, the priests shall not neglect one of them, that the enemy may not prevail over them and overcome them; for by this they drive them away at all times.
42.10: And as for those who are weak in the work of the flesh, these three prayers are not fitting for them — without the prayer of supplication; they are fitting for them, in their houses, with prayer and with prostration, that they may dwell in the house of the Christian in the morning and the evening; for it is a guard for them from Satan and his hosts, when they sleep; for there came in [a time] of making them to forget their entering in, and they know not until they awaken them; one cometh and reproveth him; and behold, Satan showeth them his form [in sleep]; swiftly he casteth them down [like] a demon, and by making them forget, and they awaken not — those who are indeed sleeping; and if a man hath prayed the prayer of supplication, he is not able — Satan — to appear unto him, nor to cast him down.
42.11: And if at all the supplication is mingled with those [prayers] — arise; these: reckon not upon them sin; for the prayer is reckoned unto them [as] falsehood, which is not [reckoned] at the completion of his days; this is the prayer which is fitting upon all the believers; but those who are weak in the work of the flesh — no — and women, freewomen, and servants, great and small.
42.12: And these one prayers: the third, and the second, and the fifth, and the half of the night are fitting for them, while they do their work.
42.13: Then they stand — or they bow down.
42.14: Or prostrate, or in every work; for God reckoneth unto them their prayers, as He reckoneth unto those who have no work; these stand and spend the night, while they watch; He said: their spending the night — God reckoneth unto them their prayer on account of their weariness in the work of the flesh, which presseth upon them; and the prayer of the morning and of the evening and of supplication are fitting for them; He addeth them with fear and trembling and prostration from them in the house of the Christian; the prayer of the morning and the evening, and the prayer of supplication in their houses; for they are not in the house of the Christian to pray — [it is] rather in their houses.
42.15: And as David the prophet said in the Psalm of the hundred and second: My soul, my soul, I will sing unto Thee.
42.16: He took away my sins from me for Thy sake; and likewise He said thus: In Thy sanctuary I appeared unto Thee, that I might behold Thy newness.
42.17: And in the Psalm: In the multitude of Thy mercy I will enter Thy house, and I will worship in the court of Thy sanctuary.
42.18: And in the Psalm of the ninth: Before Thy angels will I sing, and I will worship in the court of Thy sanctuary.
42.19: And concerning this it is fitting that the prayer of the morning and the evening be in the house of the Christian.
42.20: For these two prayers, they are the firstfruits of the day and of the night; and the prayer of supplication, let it be in the house; and these other one prayers, they pray them where a man is, in, according to the measure of their strength and by it.
42.21: For at the hour of the third hour there descended upon it the Holy Spirit upon the apostles, and they were comforted and strengthened, and He taught them all the mysteries of heaven and of earth; and it is the prayer of the Holy Spirit, and in it the believers are renewed; and in it they scourged Jesus Christ with scourgings; and at the seventh hour, in it Christ was crucified; and He saith [in] that [hour]: the tree of the Cross.
42.22: And concerning this it is fitting for us, that we pray in it unto Him who was crucified for our sake; and at the ninth hour He brought forth Adam from punishment and from the judgment of death; and in it Christ died, and broke the power of the Devil and his hosts — these are the rulers of death — and He turned Adam and his seed into Paradise; and concerning this it is fitting that we pray in it with thanksgiving and.
42.23: And in the middle of the night Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem; and in it the dead were quickened; and in it He cometh to judge the living and the dead, as He said in the holy Gospel in the parable of the ten virgins.
42.24: And concerning this it is fitting that we pray in it with work and prayer and weeping; and as for those who have in them work: they shall become [worthy of] these one [prayers] which are fitting for them, according to the measure of their strength and of their power; and if they add unto this, their joy shall be [greater]; for they are fitting, according to the measure of their strength and of their knowledge.
42.25: And if it be that in their work [they are occupied], save in the night of the Sabbath — [the night] in which those who have in them work in it — they are fitting for them likewise: the third, and the seventh, and the fifth, and the evening, upon the reading of the books; for on the day of the Sabbath Christ rose from the dead.
42.26: And concerning this He taught them, that they should glorify Him and sanctify Him in it always; and in it He cometh to judge the living and the dead; and it is fitting for them that they read His books on the day of the Sabbath wholly, that they may be ready on that great day, and may rise with Him in His glory, as they were with Him in this world; and not as the believers [are] — as the pretext of God was completed, and He shall give wealth unto him on the day of their resurrection.
42.27: So shall He rejoice with them, and give them wealth for ever on the day of their resurrection; and as He is grieved with them, and they fast two days — Wednesday and Friday — these are sad in them; His helpers, on account of the suffering and the death and the crucifixion: so shall they be delivered from grief for ever, and from hunger, and from one for ever; and He shall give them joy for ever with His helpers.

43.1: And behold, I have prepared for thee, in another book, the cause of their grief for the apostles on one day — Wednesday and Friday; and I have prepared for thee, in another book, the completion of His glory on the day of the Sabbath: how the fast of Wednesday and Friday is fitting upon all the believers — men, and women, and the young, and the small; and those who are perfected in them from their youth, this is fitting for them: for servants and for, in this week. These, friend, are not able to fast, and are not able to labour for Him who absolved them, and they are not able to do [it]; and whatever is good — if they have not kept all the three commands: for they, if they have not kept them, the power of the Holy Spirit is not with them, and they cannot do [it]; and whatever is good: for Satan striveth against them — these three commands — and He taught all the believers; and know that God shall give thee a joy which is greater than the joy of him who taketh a gift; for he who taketh a gift taketh — and who dieth not.
43.2: And do thou, by these commands, take them for the souls, from whence they sinned, and free them from the hosts, and give them life for ever; and keep thou, that thou teach men this time, without weakness; for the enemy sought to blind their hearts from their heavenly [things] and from their inward [things]; for he knoweth that by them they shall overcome him, and they shall prevail over him by their inward [things] and be strengthened; and by the reading of the holy books, and His might and His holiness — of our Lord Jesus Christ: unto Him belongeth the glory, and the holiness, and the honour, and unto His Father, and unto the Holy Spirit, now and always, unto the ages of ages. Amen.

44.1: A discourse of haste, concerning the denial of the day of the Sabbath and its completion:, friend — God shall enlighten the eyes of thy heart by the light of His holy, He comforted, that thou mayest perceive the mysteries of the kingdom.
44.2: That which I commanded thee, that I should declare unto thee the completion of the day of holiness and glory: know that it is all the work of the day of the Sabbath; it is the day of God; and its name among all the children of baptism; for all of them call it Kyriake, in the tongue of the Greeks; its interpretation: the day of God, in which He rose from the dead; and concerning this we were commanded, that we should rejoice in it with spiritual songs, in every week, and that we should not do in it the work of this world — the hosts — but that there be in it, in our gatherings of assembly, [works] for God; for it is His day; and in it [let us] work the works of God, in which the believers inherit the kingdom of God for ever, and the life which shall not pass away from being saved.
44.3: And the works of this world — for ever in them there is revealed the life for ever; thou art the life which passeth away, and the world passeth away.
44.4: God said: Work for the life of this world which passeth away.
44.5: Two days, and on the day of the Sabbath, work for Me alone; for it is My day, and I will give you your joy instead of what ye worked for Me — My kingdom for ever, and My life for ever, and My flower which fadeth not; and I will bless you in your work in the six days which ye work in it; and I will not put you into the in which ye are.
44.6: that it may be for you on My day [a recompense] for what ye worked for Me in it.
44.7: And when ye have worked for Me your desires — the three lives, and the three portions, earthly and heavenly — and as ye worked for Me [in] that which is, I separated you from my peoples and from my and from my joy for ever; and I grieved you in the work of the flesh, which ye made it; it is better than my work; and your food, which consumeth you, the which shall be for you on My day, from the of which consumeth you — or in the suffering of — I tried you in it, that ye should give all your labour.
44.8: Or they steal your, or by they your.
44.9: Or destroy your seed, or slay that which was tried from your friend; and ye shall be grieved, and ye shall be sad on earth and in heaven; for I am He who enrich eth, and I make poor and I kill and I make alive.
44.10: Friend, this is the interpretation of the word of God concerning the day of the Sabbath: that it is the day in which it is not fitting that they should do in it a work which is not without work.
44.11: And the work is: His glory — of God — and His holiness, always; and the hearing of His holy books all the day long: this is the work of God which is fitting that they should do on the day of the Sabbath, which is the day of God; and by this work the believers live a good life, which is on earth and in heaven.
44.12: And concerning this it is fitting for the believers that they keep the commandment, and rejoice [in] the work of this world, and rest from him in this.
44.13: And many of the believers neglect in this from their works for ever; they neglect God in this light; and their is greater than the of those who do the work of this world; for they do the work of this world, for they take their food in the life which passeth away, which presseth upon it, while they are in this world.
44.14: And as for those who work for God, they gain the kingdom for ever and the life which passeth not away; God neglected not on the day of the Sabbath [to turn] from earthly gain [and] loss, unto the gain — the gain for ever, heavenly.
44.15: And if we neglect the earthly works and do not the heavenly works, behold, there are lost from us the two lives together.
44.16: And they do the work of loss — gain by — from us, and our gain, neither in this world nor in the heavens.
44.17: And their — of him who neglecteth on the day of the Sabbath [to turn] from the work of this world, and doeth not the work of heaven on the day of — is greater than the of those who do in it the work of this light.
44.18: The world, and their perdition is greater than the perdition of those who — for they did not honour the day of God, and the days of this world, precious from them; for God, for the honour of His own day — His blessing — the heavenly [believers], that they should do in it the work of heaven, that their gain in it may be greater than the gain of the days [of this world]; for their gain is in two days — loss and.
44.19: And their in this day increaseth always, for ever; and the honour of this day and its exaltation is greater than [that of] two days, on account of its heavenly work; and he who gained the gain for ever on the days — the seventh — and gained not the gain of God on the day of God: behold, he sought not the day of God [to be] a help, from him who worked in it the work of this world — loss; for it is a very small gain — the gain of this world; and Paradise — he gained not in it for ever, nor in heaven; behold, verily he sought and made the two days of this world precious [away] from him.
44.20: And his is great; for he sought not the day of God, which He commanded that they should honour it.
44.21: And God increaseth [him] who sought not; and him who honoureth Me, him will I honour; and he who dishonoureth God, and doeth not unto Him work on the day of God, shall be dishonoured on earth and in heaven; and he who honoureth God on the day, and doeth unto Him work, God shall honour on earth and in heaven.
44.22: Know, friend, that all the of the books of the commandment, and all of them from this commandment; and all of them concerning it — strive, and be diligent in it, that thou mayest be saved from and mayest find the good life, which is on earth and in heaven.

45.1: And know not that the day of the Sabbath is the day of God in oldness and in life; for God wrought in it all His works in oldness and in life; man, it was not revealed unto thee from this, in oldness, He said: the Book of Creation — the head of the earth — that in it God wrought all His creations, as He revealed unto thee in the Book of the Interpretation of the Incarnation for the Son of God, and His seed.
45.2: And I, man, will not declare unto thee again a time, that thou mayest make known unto him who perceiveth not the desire of the book.
45.3: And God said in the Book of Creation, which rested — He said: His hand is unto Moses, the chief of His prophets — Work ye: on the day of the Sabbath He made heaven for the day in which are the spiritual angels; and in it He created all their orders.
45.4: And in it He created heaven and all that is in it.
45.5: And in it He made the light; and in it the one nature of those whom He created on the day of the Sabbath.
45.6: For on the day of the Sabbath He created heaven, for Him who separated — that which He created — in the beginning of the Sabbath.
45.7: And on the third day He created all [things] in the of the earth, which He created on the day of the Sabbath.
45.8: And on the fourth day He created the sun and the moon and the stars, from the light which He created on the day of the Sabbath.
45.9: And on the fifth day He created the fishes and the birds and the fowl, from the water which He created on the day of the Sabbath.
45.10: And on the day of Friday He created the beasts and the wild beasts that move, from the earth which He created on the day of the Sabbath.
45.11: And in it was their work: He made Adam, and for Eve He created their body from the four natures which He created for them on the day of the Sabbath.
45.12: And He created their soul, as an entrance, from the light which He created for them on the day of the Sabbath.
45.13: And on the day of the Sabbath God did all the work; it is the day of God in oldness, which He wrought in it.
45.15: the heart of him who declareth not unto anything on the day of the Sabbath, declareth: our Lord Jesus Christ, who was born of, the holy Virgin, and there shone forth a light — He said — [upon] the earth, as He created the light on the day of the Sabbath.
45.16: And in it He appeared, that He is Christ, the King of the Jews, whom they await: when He entered Jerusalem, they took palm branches in their hands, He said, and all the Jews believed in Him, and Hosanna — while they say: Hosanna to the Son of David, whose interpretation is: for the name of Jesus in their tongue, its interpretation is Saviour.
45.17: And on the day of the Sabbath He was called again, on this day, the Holy [One]; and on the day of the Sabbath He rose from the dead, and gave life unto the souls of all the children of Adam, who were dead in Sheol, and brought them up into the rest for ever, into the Paradise of joy.
45.18: And on the eighth day after His resurrection He declared again unto His disciples that He is risen in His body.
45.19: When Thomas put his hand into His side, and in it they were convinced — all those who believed in Him — of that which they saw.
45.20: And on the day of the Sabbath was the feast of the fourth — the Holy Spirit — upon His disciples; and He made them of God and of His Father, and His brethren, and partakers with Him in the kingdom; and He made us unto them, and unto all those who are baptized with His baptism and believe in their; and swiftly on the day of the Sabbath, in which there descended upon them the Holy Spirit, [there was] preaching in Christ unto the Jews who were in Jerusalem, until there believed from them souls; and after that from their holiness, and it is the day of of God, and the day of faith; and in it we were commanded that our bodies should be for us for the life for ever, and that we should rejoice with Him in the joy for ever; and it is the day of God, in which He did all the work in oldness and in life, and it is the day of rest, and which is for ever in it, and the day of His resurrection and of the resurrection of all creation; and it is the day of the kingdom which is first, and which.
45.21: And it is the head of the days which are unto Him in this world and in; and commanded us concerning it, that we should not do in it a work which is not without work, and should not neglect the work; and in it [men] hasten after this His work — His glory and His holiness, and the reading of His books — always, from morning until evening.
45.22: And He ordained — the soul which doeth not this work thus, always, on the day of the Sabbath, shall go forth from the people; and I have declared unto thee that which [is] of this incarnation.
45.23: And concerning it, God taught all who were found of all the believers — one, and the nations of servants, and the — that they should keep [it] and do [it], and should be saved from destruction for ever, and should seek the life of the kingdom for ever.
45.24: And he who kept it not, as I said unto thee — behold — that the nations our Lord by His: that which is hidden from our Lord; and as for thee — for [it is] the name of his Lord.
45.25: And as for thee: for God saith unto them with one word of the words: I, in two days created — by one word — all creation; and on the seventh day I rested from all My work; and I blessed it — the seventh day — I hallowed it, for in it I rested.
45.26: And then shall a man rest on that day, and shall give rest unto the man, and unto the son, and unto the, and unto his servant, and unto his maidservant, and and the stranger who dwelleth in the house; and every soul which resteth not on that day, that soul shall be cut off from her people: this word — its name by its — by one word.
45.27: And they did the work which He commanded them in it all their days, and transgressed not Thy commandment: when they found a man gathering sticks on the day of the Sabbath, they asked the sticks how they should do in it; and He commanded that they should stone him with stones, that he should die.
45.28: What is it that God, in it, when He created creation in two days? He rested not; He rested on the day of the first [day], and magnified thus; and He commanded them that they should rest with Him in it; everyone who hath understanding knoweth that He fainted not in doing creation; for swiftly He completeth, without weariness.
45.29: And if He fainted not, neither rested He again; for He rested — [He] saith — [He] declareth unto us concerning weariness; it was before rest. And if He fainted not, and rested not again, He magnified this commandment thus unto everyone who resteth not with Him.
45.30: And how much more [punishment] was decreed upon everyone who resteth not with Him on the day of the Sabbath, which is the day of rest in truth.
45.31: And he who knew, in his ignorance, weariness and rest — his name is He who, before the day of the first [day], fainted not in the creation of His creations, and rested not again in it on account of weariness; and He rested — [He] saith — He knew by this: weariness in truth, and rest in truth, which was on the day of the Sabbath; for Christ, the Word of God who was incarnate, is He who created His creations; for God in it created all the work, and fainted not in the creation of His creations; for He was not fleshly, and fainted not; and He was not fleshly, and weariness came not [upon Him] by that which He doeth; but He doeth all the work without weariness, by His will; and He was incarnate, and I — unto Him [are] flesh and blood; and they chose Him — and for the — and He was wearied for our sake; weariness in truth, from before the day of the Sabbath, until by His soul; and on the day of the Sabbath He rested, and gave us rest with Him; for He, in the night of Friday, gave up His head for our sake, by His will, unto suffering; and He endured weariness for our sake; and they bound Him, and took Him unto the court of the chief priest; and they sat that night all of it; they mocked Him, and smote Him, and cast spittle into His face.

46.1: And the dusk of the day of Friday: they loosed [Him] against Him in death, and delivered Him up to him who knew not, the governor of Rome; and they spake concerning Him, that he willeth to take the kingdom for himself; and they subjected [Him] to the hosts of the governor over Him in the assembly; their word [was] until they scourged Him, and they mocked Him, as they mock, until they cried out among kings.
46.2: And again they crucified Him upon the tree, and pierced His hands and His feet; and while they mocked Him concerning the everlasting kingdom.
46.3: And they were troubled in toil and in silence, and were able, and they made themselves ready in this with wrath, until He died for us by His will, in the thoughts of the day of Friday; and after the remembrance of the body, until the going down, they buried Him in the sepulchre, as the dead, on the day of the eve.
46.4: And on the day of the Sabbath the dead were sought, and He brought up all the souls which were in the toil of Sheol, and He led them into Paradise, and He gave them rest in everlasting joy: the soul of Adam, and the soul of all his seed which was born from the earth, forty and four and two hundred forty and four years; He rested from his toil, and He gave rest also unto all his seed from toil for ever. This is the day of rest in truth, for Him, and for all who keep watch, Adam, those who were formed, as He showed him, and their Creator; and not as they in the creation of creations; and not as the rest on the first day. Behold, make thou able with the ears of thy heart our knowledge in the midst of this toil and the rest, rest from the toil of rest.
46.5: And woe unto him who is an offence unto him to whom it is fitting: for him who resteth not on this day — utterly, from his offence — for him who resteth not on the first day; for he is [one] who, when he was made, [there was] offence and destruction upon the soul which resteth not with him on the day which is spent therein, and doth not rest the rest which is in truth.
46.6: Blessed [is] the beloved; for the man who resteth not on this day is cut off from his people, unto Christ.
46.7: And a father of witnesses shall fall; and blessed [is] he who standeth: the rest is not this which thou blamest from His work, alone; those who have believed the Sabbaths and for them: and they read the Holy Scriptures on the day of the Sabbath, all of them — this is its work; he shall take the spirit of life, and the everlasting possession, which is better than the work of the world, wherein he taketh life, life.
46.8: For God saith: the Rest — this is it — the flesh resteth not, but [it is] the rest of the soul.
46.9: For He, on this day, rested the souls which were shut up in Sheol, from their toil, for ever therein.
46.10: And therein it is fitting for the believers that their souls rest in the glory of God and in His holiness, and that they hear His word every day; for I have written for thee in the book as a likeness; Simeon — for the believers — that God made the soul of man as the angels, and his flesh as the beasts; and if the soul sinneth — glory and holiness and the hearing of the word of God — it dieth from the life of God for ever, as the flesh dieth from life, destruction; if it sinneth, spoiled and spent, in the rest of the flesh, as the flesh of the beasts; and the word of God, it is the rest of the soul, as it is fitting.
46.11: And concerning this God saith: Make ye two days for the life of the flesh of the beast, as it is gathered together.
46.12: He sought for life: of asses [was] for Him; make ye for the life of the soul which liveth, as it is gathered together: an enclosure for the soul; and this shall be that which is better than this — it is gathered together; He sought for the ass; for He is [He] who, when He gathered together for the ass, He sought, and gathered not together for the soul — an enclosure — from it; and he took not [away]; the ass shall live from his; and they shall not be able to live.
46.13: And if He gather together an enclosure for the soul first, [there is] life; and He is [He] who is able, according to the measure that there is life, as; it is gathered together; He sought for the ass.
46.14: And concerning this our God saith: He sought first my kingdom and my righteousness; and take ye no thought for all which is desired from the work of the world.
46.15: He is able — that which is joined unto His glory, unto His holiness and unto the hearing of His word; the of his soul [is] life everlasting; God giveth unto him who willeth from the work of the world; these and He in the being joined unto His glory and His holiness; for the bread is in His hand, and He is upon all work; and He is [He] who in; and He giveth a hand unto him who is commanded, unto him.

47.1: And now I love, O beloved, as the word of God, which saith: men shall rest on the day of the Sabbath — this which saith that he be joined unto His glory and unto His holiness and unto the hearing of His word, every day, both of them; and if he hath been made from this, in the life of the flesh of men, and concerning death, before the day of the Sabbath, the other — he shall perish from the people of God; and they which is gathered together for his flesh, beastly, from destruction; behold, he slept, that and a dead soul; and he caused to sleep, and God, salvation, who chose life from the life of his soul.
47.2: And if he concerning that which he did, and God shall quicken [him] until the day of the Sabbath, the other; and [he] shall be joined unto that which is commanded therein: the life of his soul, rest from the sin which was fitted upon him on the day of his being joined, for the servant of God, on the day which He chose for his soul from the seven days, the other.
47.3: God saith: men shall rest therein, and shall be joined unto the glory and unto the holiness and unto the reading, and shall not be made from Him in the work of the world.
47.4: He saith: and if he hath been made from Him in the work of destruction, and hath been from Him, he shall perish from the people of God, as God saith: Every soul which resteth not on that day shall be separated from His people — this which saith, as a cup they shall the of the people of strangers.
47.5: And concerning this it is fitting for them, that they on the day of the Sabbath unto the house of the Christians, the Paradise of God, and be joined unto the glory and the holiness which is without toil, and [that] which is without work, for the servant of destruction.
47.6: And from the ordinance of the offering, he shall be joined unto the reading of the books of God every day, both, for it is the day of God.
47.7: God saith by the tongue of David the prophet in the Psalm, the account of two and two: this is it — the day which God made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.

48.1: This which saith, in joy: spiritual is he who is in the reading of the books of God, which is the rest of the soul, and life, and thy joy: as God said — for man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word which proceedeth out of the mouth of God; for the word of God, it is the life of thy spirit, as the bread is the life of the flesh.
48.2: And if there be a man who loveth a companion for him who heareth the reading of God, God giveth the portion of the righteous [in] His reading in the kingdom of heaven; and the portion shall be that which is greater than the portion which taketh up the dead; and in the first [place] he is greater than in the first [place], he.
48.3: For he who taketh up the dead shall take up the body which is present [and] shall die.
48.4: And as for him who readeth the word of God on the day of the Sabbath, he shall take up souls from their sins, that they may live unto everlasting; and the alms of this are greater than the alms of him who spendeth upon the orthodox; and He satisfieth them, for He is [He who] filled and watered the perishing flesh and the perishing
48.5: And this, moreover, satisfieth the soul and watereth [it], which liveth for ever.
48.6: How much is he who taketh up, who readeth on the day of God the word of God, for him who causeth [others] to hear the reading.
48.7: And as for him who knoweth not the reading, it is fitting for him to go unto him who causeth [others] to hear the reading, without toil.
48.8: And if he be not in the city in which he dwelleth, [in] that [place] where [one] causeth [others] to hear the reading, he shall go unto another city where [one] causeth [others] to hear the reading, as he goeth for the sake of a perishing work, from a city which hath no market unto another city in which there is a market; and he who from the life of the soul shall perish from God, as his flesh perisheth, which in the work of the life of his flesh, from the life of this world.
48.9: This is the reason of the Sabbath.
48.10: And as for him who doeth not a spiritual work, he shall be lost from the life everlasting, and from the life of this world.
48.11: For he who abideth in a perishing work, from a spiritual work, on the day of the Sabbath, hath destroyed the soul, and shall be lost from the life everlasting; and God shall judge him on the day of the third and in sorrow, in earth and in heaven, as He said: By the hand of; and it was not.
48.12: If ye keep the commandment on the day of the Sabbath, God giveth life and good, and much is His power; and He unto him always in earth and in heaven; and God giveth on two days great things, the which they on that day; and He blesseth, and therein.
48.13: God saith: men shall rest on this day; and men shall rest with Him; and the son and the daughter and the manservant and the maidservant shall rest.
48.14: And concerning this, it is fitting for a man that he work not, for a woman, the work of the world, and that he not diminish the glory of God and the holiness of God, but that he go with the woman unto God and unto the house of the Christians; and he shall rest in the voice of God; and so shall he do for our sons and our daughters and our servants and our maidservants and the stranger who dwelleth in the house; and he shall not make them [do] the work of the world. And as for him who resteth not, he [is] in the hearing of the word of God alone; and God shall seek blood from his hand; for he is a good rest for the soul alone; but it is fitting for him that he be grieved concerning their former state, as a soul; and He shall make good unto them in the being joined unto the glory of God and unto the holiness and unto the hearing of His word; and they shall not be made in the work of: the work of the flesh, except that which they keep for food alone.
48.15: And as for that which is food and drink, which the flesh cannot [do] without it, they shall do this in the night, before the glory and the holiness.
48.16: And if they are able, they shall do this on the day before; for God them in this until the evening.
48.17: For He saith: I rested, and men rested; and our sons and our servants and our maidservants and the stranger, who is his house, rested; and our asses rested; and the rest of the asses — which He saith — is the rest of His flesh; that is: our asses are the soul.
48.18: And He commanded that [a man] rest not with food and drink on the day of the Sabbath, which is the day of rest, that the being joined unto the reading every day, both of them; and the righteous and joy shall; for He is [He] who, when He was hungry, for the souls in hunger, and shall from life.

49.1: And concerning this, God commanded that we eat and drink and rejoice on the Sabbath day in full; and He commanded concerning the flesh — its name is the flesh of beasts, mingled — and He appointed a day for us, for the day; and it is confirmed by this word of God: He appointed for the flesh, food and drink; goeth forth for the work of the Spirit on the Sabbath day; and He appointed upon it, in rest.
49.2: Behold, I have loved that which I have revealed unto thee; and take heed in thy heart, and teach them the name of the Faith, and unto others; for it is the foundation of the life which is eternal, and of the life of this world; and they rooted it in [the two] in earth and in heaven; and [there is] deliverance from judgment, and rest from the two works of toil, and riches from the hidden treasures in earth and in heaven.
49.3: For thou knowest that which is written in [the book of] the Kings: that God appeared unto Solomon, and said unto him: Ask of Me that which I shall give thee.
49.4: And Solomon said unto Him: I have asked of Thee that Thou wouldest give me a wise heart, that I may judge aright in the midst of this great people.
49.5: The Scripture saith: And God was pleased at this word; for he asked of Him a heavenly work, which abideth, and he asked not of Him an earthly work, which perisheth.
49.6: And God said unto him: Because thou hast asked neither length of days, nor abundance of riches, nor the soul of thine enemies, but thou hast asked wisdom — and it is the work which pleaseth Me — behold, I give thee the wisdom which thou hast asked of Me, which I have given unto none before thee, neither after thee.
49.7: And I will add unto thee, above this, that which thou hast not asked of Me: length of days, and abundance of riches, and the soul of thine enemies.
49.8: Behold, I have loved how Solomon, when he desired the work which abideth alone, and sought not the work which perisheth, God gave him the abiding [thing] which he had asked, and added unto him, above this, the perishing work which he had not asked; for He knew that which he desired.
49.9: And likewise He saith in the Gospel: Seek ye My kingdom and My righteousness, and I will add unto you that which ye desire of the work of this world, which is food and drink and clothing.
49.10: Likewise everyone who laboureth for the glory of God and His holiness, and heareth His word on the Sabbath day in full, shall obtain in this kingdom of heaven: God shall give that [portion], and shall grant him good and rest from all that wearieth, from the work of this world — food and drink and clothing — as He did unto Solomon. And he who laboureth not thus for the life of his soul, from the eternal kingdom, but inheriteth eternal judgment — God shall afflict him in this world, and shall weary him all the days of his life, and shall deprive him of the two rests together, in heaven and in earth; for God is mighty and able.
49.11: And he who laboureth for the day of the LORD, and shall be exalted with the LORD on the day of His resurrection in full — he also shall abide with the LORD on the day of the resurrection; he shall be exalted on the day of glory and honour, as it was done on earth on the Sabbath day. And he who laboureth not for the glory of God and His holiness, and heareth not His word on the Sabbath day, shall go forth from the fathers of God and from His glory, as the Devil fell when he was withheld from glory and holiness on the Sabbath day: lo, they are in it — they fell; and in it shall fall all who labour not for the glory of God and His holiness, as they fell.
49.12: And behold, I have revealed unto thee in the book of Kasit, the spiritual writing, that for those who are weak in work, their portion is appointed upon them on the Sabbath day; and it is appointed for glory and for holiness at the times, twice on the Sabbath day: the morning, and two and a hundred and four, and the evening, within, upon the day which is read, all the day; for when they are steadfast [refraining] from the perishing work, it is fitting for them that they be joined unto prayer at the times, within, upon the day which is read.
49.13: And on the two days also, the others — it is not fitting for them save for eating; it is not fitting for them save for eating, in the book — as I have shown thee in the book of Helit of the host: they shall pray wheresoever they are, according to the measure of their strength and their knowledge, if they do not their work; and God hearkened unto them.
49.14: I have loved: behold, I have shown thee the glory of the Sabbath day; and in it is the life of the faithful, and their joy which is in earth and in heaven is upon them, and work is therein; and teach all whom thou hast found, [unto them], the faithful; and behold, I have revealed unto thee the reason of the fast: one day, Wednesday and Friday, in the peace of God. Amen.

50.1: The second discourse, concerning the ordinances of the fast of the one day, Wednesday and Friday, which is the love of God: may He enlighten the eyes of thy heart by the light of the Holy Spirit, the Comforter, that thou mayest discern the mystery of the Godhead.
50.2: I have agreed with thee that I would reveal unto thee the ordinances of the fast of the one day, Wednesday and Friday; there is that which I have told thee; and know its meaning, and hold fast, as the fathers, the holy apostles, said in their canons — the seventh and the tenth — whoso fasteth not the one day —
